issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter missing @MainActor annotation
issues.description: The rule requires that classes interacting with UIKit or performing UI updates must be marked with @MainActor annotation. The SettingsTextFormatter class formats text for UI display in settings screens but lacks the @MainActor annotation.
issues.rule_name: UI-Related Code Must Be Annotated with @MainActor

issues.title: Incorrect localized string reference in SettingsTextFormatter
issues.description: The formatStudiesText method references strings.detailTextStudies instead of strings.detailTextStudiesV2. This causes the formatter to display the old v1 Studies message ('%@ may install and run studies from time to time.') instead of the new v148 message ('%@ randomly selects users to test features, which improves quality for everyone.') that was added in this PR. The helper class was clearly intended to format the new v148 strings based on the PR context, but uses the wrong string constant.

issues.title: Inconsistent format specifier documentation in RolloutsSettingMessage comment
issues.description: The comment for RolloutsSettingMessage incorrectly documents the format specifier as '%1$@' (positional format) while the actual value string uses '%@' (simple format). This mismatch creates confusion for localization teams and could lead to incorrect translations, as translators may attempt to use positional formatting based on the comment when the string implementation doesn't support it. The comment should match the actual format specifier used in the value field.

issues.title: Linter exclusion points to wrong message key version
issues.description: The linter configuration exclusion was updated to reference 'Settings.Studies.Message.v148' but the original PR added this key to exclude quotes validation for the v136 message. Since the PR adds new v148 strings with similar content containing quotes, the exclusion should have remained as v136 to maintain the existing exclusion, or both versions should be excluded. This change will cause the linter to fail validation on the v136 string that legitimately needs the exclusion, while potentially missing issues in the new v148 string.

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter class missing final keyword
issues.description: The newly added SettingsTextFormatter class violates repository Rule #12 from AGENTS.md, which requires classes that are not designed for subclassing to be marked with the 'final' keyword. This helper class is clearly not intended for inheritance (it has a private initializer and is a simple utility class), but lacks the final modifier. This prevents compiler optimizations and fails to communicate design intent explicitly, violating an explicit compliance rule added in this same PR.

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter and its methods lack explicit access control
issues.description: Rule requires explicit access control modifiers. The new nested class and its members use default (implicit) access levels (`class`, `static let shared`, and `func` declarations have no explicit `internal`/`private`/`public`).
issues.rule_name: Properties and Methods Must Have Appropriate Access Control

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter should be marked final
issues.description: The helper singleton class is not designed for inheritance but is declared as a non-final class. Per the rule, such classes must be marked `final` to prevent unintended subclassing and enable compiler optimizations.
issues.rule_name: Classes That Should Not Be Subclassed Must Be Marked Final

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31198 - EXP-5874 Add strings for Rollouts toggle and update Studies strings

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds localization strings for a new Rollouts toggle feature and updates existing Studies strings in both Firefox iOS and Firefox Focus iOS apps. The changes include:

1. In `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift`: Adds new string constants for Studies v3 and Rollouts toggle UI elements (title, link, message)
2. In `firefox-ios/Shared/Supporting Files/`: Updates en-CA and en-GB localization files with new v148 strings
3. In `.github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json`: Adds exclusion for `Settings.Studies.Message.v148` in quotes linter
4. In `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift`: Adds new string constants for Studies v2 and Rollouts, plus a new `SettingsTextFormatter` helper class

The PR is preparatory work for splitting the studies toggle into separate Studies and Rollouts toggles as mentioned in the description referencing PR #30988.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The PR introduces a `SettingsTextFormatter` class in focus-ios that is not being used by the current codebase - `SettingsViewController.swift` still uses the old direct string formatting pattern. This creates dead code and inconsistency. Additionally, the new strings are defined but not integrated into the UI, leaving them unused. There's also a mismatch between the v148 string versions added to firefox-ios and the v2 versions added to focus-ios for similar functionality.

architecture.overview: The PR extends the localization infrastructure for the Firefox Focus and Firefox iOS apps by adding new string constants for the v148 release. In firefox-ios, it adds Studies v3 and Rollouts string variants. In focus-ios, it adds Studies v2 and Rollouts string variants along with a new SettingsTextFormatter helper class. The architecture shows two parallel codebases sharing similar string patterns but with different versioning schemes (v148 vs v2). The SettingsTextFormatter class was added but is not currently consumed anywhere in the codebase.
steps: 1. Existing SettingsViewController uses UIConstants.strings.detailTextStudies and UIConstants.strings.labelStudies directly
2. PR adds new strings (labelStudiesV2, detailTextStudiesV2, labelRollouts, detailTextRollouts) to focus-ios UIConstants
3. PR adds SettingsTextFormatter class with formatStudiesText and formatRolloutsText methods
4. SettingsTextFormatter is not referenced anywhere - dead code
5. SettingsViewController continues to use the old direct String(format:...) pattern
6. firefox-ios gets v148 versioned strings that appear to align with focus-ios v2 strings but use different naming

findings.title: Unused new string constants in focus-ios
findings.body:
The PR adds new string constants to `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift` (lines 206-209):
- `labelStudiesV2`
- `detailTextStudiesV2` 
- `labelRollouts`

However, `SettingsViewController.swift` (lines 127-128) still uses the old `labelStudies` and `detailTextStudies` strings directly. The new v2 strings are not referenced anywhere, making them dead code.

Either update SettingsViewController to use the new strings, or remove them if they're not ready for use yet.

findings.fixPrompt: In focus-ios/Blockzilla/Settings/Controller/SettingsViewController.swift, the initializeToggles method (lines 127-128) currently uses UIConstants.strings.labelStudies and detailTextStudies directly. If the v2 strings (labelStudiesV2, detailTextStudiesV2, labelRollouts, detailTextRollouts) added in UIConstants.swift are meant to replace these, update SettingsViewController to use the new strings. findings.title: Inconsistent versioning between firefox-ios and focus-ios
findings.body:
The PR uses different versioning schemes for similar functionality across the two codebases:

- **firefox-ios**: Uses `v148` suffix (e.g., `Settings.Studies.Title.v148`, `Settings.Rollouts.Title.v148`)
- **focus-ios**: Uses `v2` suffix (e.g., `Settings.toggleStudies.v2`, `Settings.detailTextStudies.v2`)

While not necessarily wrong, this inconsistency could confuse developers about which versioning scheme to use and may indicate the changes were not coordinated. Consider documenting the versioning convention or aligning the approach.

Also notable: The `firefox-ios` changes add `v148` strings to the main `Strings.swift` file, while `focus-ios` adds `v2` strings to `UIConstants.swift` - different patterns for similar functionality.
findings.fixPrompt: Review the versioning scheme for string constants across firefox-ios and focus-ios. firefox-ios uses v148 suffix (Settings.Studies.Title.v148) while focus-ios uses v2 (Settings.toggleStudies.v2). Document or align on a consistent versioning convention for future string additions to avoid confusion.

findings.title: Missing Tests for SettingsTextFormatter
findings.body:
No tests were added for the new string constants or the SettingsTextFormatter class. While string files are typically tested through localization testing, the new SettingsTextFormatter helper class in focus-ios would benefit from unit tests to verify correct string formatting with different app names.

Consider adding tests for:
- SettingsTextFormatter.formatStudiesText returns correctly formatted string
- SettingsTextFormatter.formatRolloutsText returns correctly formatted string

Without tests, there's no automated verification that these formatters continue to work correctly as the code evolves.
findings.fixPrompt: Add unit tests for SettingsTextFormatter in focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift to verify formatStudiesText and formatRolloutsText methods return correctly formatted strings with different app names. Look at existing XCUITest or unit test patterns in focus-ios for guidance.

findings.title: Positive: String constants properly documented
findings.body:
The new string constants in both files include clear comments explaining their purpose, such as:
- "Label used as a toggle item in Settings. When this is off, the user is opting out of all rollouts."
- "A short description that explains that Mozilla may change features remotely. %1$@ is the app name (e.g. Firefox)."

This is good practice for localization strings and helps translators and developers understand the context.
